articles.title: Mega-Sena 3080 pode pagar R$ 42 milhões neste domingo; g1 transmite | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado. Já os Bolões CAIXA nos canais eletrônicos ocorrem até as 10h45.
articles.summary: Apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado. Já os Bolões CAIXA nos canais eletrônicos ocorrem até as 10h45.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.080 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 42 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 11h deste domingo (1º), em São Paulo.

No concurso da última sexta-feira (30), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Os principais temas das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Inflação, política migratória e desgaste de Trump também pesam na disputa pelo Congresso, enquanto inteligência artificial ganha espaço inédito na campanha.
articles.summary: Inflação, política migratória e desgaste de Trump também pesam na disputa pelo Congresso, enquanto inteligência artificial ganha espaço inédito na campanha.
articles.body:
A guerra contra o Irã , o custo de vida, a inteligência artificial e a imigração estão entre os principais temas da campanha para as eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos . Os assuntos devem pesar na decisão dos eleitores na votação de 3 de novembro .

A uma semana do pleito, estas são as principais preocupações dos americanos:

O custo de vida é, sem dúvida, o principal tema destas eleições e aparece nos discursos de democratas e republicanos.

Na campanha de 2024, Donald Trump criticou a inflação elevada e responsabilizou o então presidente Joe Biden pelo aumento dos preços.

Quase dois anos depois de retornar à Casa Branca, porém, o republicano ainda não conseguiu conter a alta, que afeta desde os combustíveis e os aluguéis até os produtos vendidos nos supermercados .

O cenário também é agravado pela guerra comercial de Trump , baseada na imposição de tarifas sobre produtos importados de diversos países, incluindo aliados e parceiros dos Estados Unidos .

Em pesquisa divulgada na última segunda-feira (26) pela CBS News, mais da metade dos americanos entrevistados afirmou que sua situação financeira piorou em consequência das políticas econômicas do presidente .

Uma urna eletrônica na eleição para governador na Virgínia, nos Estados Unidos — Foto: LightRocket via Getty Images, via BBC

A guerra contra o Irã , iniciada por Trump em conjunto com Israel, não conquistou amplo apoio entre os americanos.

Nos primeiros dias do conflito, cerca de 40% dos americanos apoiavam a guerra, enquanto 49% eram contrários, segundo a média de pesquisas compilada pelo especialista Nate Silver.

Atualmente, o apoio caiu para 35% , enquanto 55% dos entrevistados se dizem contrários ao conflito.

A disparada dos preços dos combustíveis também contribui para a rejeição à guerra. Entre os fatores que pressionaram o mercado de energia está o fechamento do Estreito de Ormuz durante o conflito.

Uma pesquisa da Universidade Emerson, realizada em setembro, apontou a guerra como a principal preocupação dos eleitores.

Embora Trump tenha feito campanha com a promessa de deportar imigrantes em situação irregular, a política migratória se mostrou mais complexa do que o previsto. A atuação dos agentes do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega (ICE, na sigla em inglês) passou a ser alvo de críticas por causa de operações consideradas excessivas, algumas delas com mortes.

Trump conseguiu reduzir o fluxo de migrantes na fronteira com o México, mas a opinião pública continua dividida sobre sua política migratória. Pesquisa da Fox News realizada no início de outubro mostrou que 43% dos americanos aprovavam a condução do tema pelo presidente, enquanto 56% desaprovavam.

Levantamento do Instituto Marist, realizado no fim de setembro, também indicou que os eleitores passaram a confiar mais nos democratas do que nos republicanos para lidar com a imigração. A mudança representa uma inversão significativa em relação a 2024.

As eleições de meio de mandato tradicionalmente funcionam como um referendo sobre o presidente em exercício. Neste ano, Trump também está no centro da disputa.

Enquanto presidentes costumam adotar uma postura mais discreta durante as campanhas legislativas, Trump, de 80 anos, pediu aos eleitores que votem como se seu próprio nome estivesse nas cédulas em 3 de novembro.

O republicano, no entanto, enfrenta seu pior momento de popularidade . Parte dos americanos também defende mecanismos mais rigorosos de controle sobre os poderes do presidente.

Questões relacionadas à ética no governo estão entre as principais preocupações dos eleitores, segundo uma pesquisa do Pew Research Center.

Os democratas prometeram abrir uma série de investigações contra Trump e seus aliados mais próximos caso conquistem a maioria no Congresso. O partido acusa integrantes do governo de usar a Casa Branca para obter vantagens financeiras pessoais.

Inteligência artificial preocupa eleitores

A inteligência artificial aparece pela primeira vez como um tema relevante nas campanhas para as eleições de meio de mandato.

Quase metade dos americanos entrevistados pelo Pew Research Center afirmou estar muito preocupada com os efeitos da tecnologia sobre a economia.

A expansão acelerada dos centros de dados, estruturas necessárias para o desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial, também provoca resistência. O principal motivo é o elevado consumo de energia dessas instalações , que pode pressionar as contas de luz dos moradores das regiões onde são construídas.

Guerras culturais perdem espaço, mas continuam na campanha

As chamadas guerras culturais aparecem com menos frequência do que em eleições anteriores, mas continuam presentes no debate político.

Os republicanos, em particular, têm produzido peças de campanha para atacar os democratas por suas posições sobre os direitos das pessoas transgênero. Um dos principais alvos é o apoio do partido à participação de mulheres trans em competições esportivas femininas.

articles.title: Novas regras do vale-refeição e vale-alimentação passam a valer integralmente; veja detalhes | G1
articles.standfirst: Cartões de diferentes operadoras poderão ser aceitos na mesma rede. Veja o que muda para trabalhadores e comerciantes.
articles.summary: Cartões de diferentes operadoras poderão ser aceitos na mesma rede. Veja o que muda para trabalhadores e comerciantes.
articles.body:
As novas regras do vale-refeição (VR) e do vale-alimentação (VA) passam a valer neste domingo (1º), com a chamada interoperabilidade , que permite que os cartões de diferentes operadoras sejam aceitos em uma rede maior de estabelecimentos.

🔎 O objetivo é aumentar a concorrência entre as empresas que administram os benefícios e reduzir os custos para restaurantes, supermercados e outros estabelecimentos comerciais.

➡️ Mas o que muda para os trabalhadores? O vale-refeição poderá ser usado em supermercados? E o vale-alimentação, em restaurantes? Será possível sacar o dinheiro dos cartões? As empresas são obrigadas a oferecer esses benefícios?

Para esclarecer essas e outras dúvidas, o g1 ouviu Elber Laranja, engenheiro de produtos de crédito, e consultou a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho (AFT).

vale-refeição e vale-alimentação — Foto: Freepik

A interoperabilidade permite que as empresas que administram vale-refeição e vale-alimentação compartilhem suas redes de estabelecimentos credenciados.

🔎 Na prática, a medida busca resolver um problema comum: chegar a um restaurante, supermercado ou lanchonete e descobrir que o local aceita vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação, mas não a bandeira do seu cartão .

Com a interoperabilidade plena, as redes passam a funcionar de forma integrada. Assim, um estabelecimento poderá aceitar cartões de diferentes operadoras utilizando a mesma estrutura de pagamento, sem precisar contratar cada empresa separadamente.

O trabalhador deverá encontrar mais estabelecimentos que aceitam seu vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação , independentemente da bandeira do cartão.

A mudança, porém, não aumenta o saldo dos cartões, não permite transformar o benefício em dinheiro nem amplia os tipos de produtos que podem ser comprados.

🔎 Segundo Elber, o trabalhador terá mais facilidade para usar os cartões, mas continuará sujeito às mesmas regras sobre o que pode comprar com cada benefício.

O vale-refeição poderá ser usado em supermercados?

Não. Embora os cartões passem a ser aceitos em mais estabelecimentos, isso não muda as regras sobre o uso dos benefícios.

🔎 O que está sendo ampliado é a rede de locais que aceitam os cartões , mantendo a finalidade de cada benefício.

O vale-refeição continua destinado à compra de refeições prontas, como almoços , jantares e lanches , em restaurantes , lanchonetes , padarias e estabelecimentos semelhantes.

Já o vale-alimentação continua destinado à compra de alimentos , como os vendidos em supermercados e mercearias .

Posso comprar eletrônicos, medicamentos e outros produtos em supermercados?

Não. Segundo Elber, mesmo que supermercados, farmácias, postos de combustível e lojas de conveniência vendam alimentos, os cartões continuam destinados exclusivamente a despesas com alimentação.

Os benefícios não podem ser usados para comprar medicamentos, combustíveis, cosméticos, produtos de higiene, eletrônicos ou outros produtos que não sejam alimentos.

A regra também vale para supermercados. Mesmo que esses estabelecimentos vendam eletrodomésticos, celulares, brinquedos, roupas e utensílios domésticos, esses produtos não podem ser pagos com vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação.

As regras do PAT determinam que os recursos sejam utilizados para a alimentação do trabalhador.

Por isso, produtos que não atendam a essa finalidade, como bebidas alcoólicas, podem ser considerados incompatíveis com as regras do programa durante fiscalizações dos órgãos responsáveis.

Não. O dinheiro depositado pela empresa continua destinado exclusivamente à alimentação e não pode ser movimentado livremente como o saldo de uma conta bancária.

O trabalhador não pode sacar o saldo, transferir os valores para uma conta bancária nem utilizar outros meios para transformar o benefício em dinheiro.

🔎 Segundo Elber, acordos informais entre trabalhadores e comerciantes para trocar o saldo dos cartões por dinheiro continuam sendo irregulares .

Posso transferir o saldo para outra pessoa ou entre benefícios?

Não. Quem recebe os dois benefícios continuará tendo um saldo específico para vale-refeição e outro para vale-alimentação.

Não será permitido transferir dinheiro de um benefício para o outro nem enviar os valores para outras pessoas.

As novas regras também valem para aplicativos de delivery?

Sim. As regras continuam valendo independentemente de a compra ser feita presencialmente ou pela internet.

Os cartões multibenefícios serão proibidos?

Não. As empresas poderão continuar oferecendo cartões que reúnem diferentes benefícios em um único meio de pagamento.

A diferença é que os valores destinados à alimentação deverão ficar separados dos saldos de outros benefícios disponíveis no mesmo cartão.

🔎 Segundo Elber, os valores de vale-refeição e vale-alimentação vinculados ao PAT deverão continuar identificados e sujeitos às regras do programa. Já os demais benefícios poderão seguir normas diferentes.

Os estabelecimentos serão obrigados a aceitar vale-refeição e vale-alimentação?

Não. Cada estabelecimento continuará podendo decidir se aceita ou não vale-refeição e vale-alimentação.

Para os estabelecimentos que já aceitam esses benefícios, porém, a tendência é que as restrições relacionadas às diferentes bandeiras diminuam.

O primeiro passo é confirmar se o estabelecimento aceita vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação.

Se o estabelecimento aceitar o benefício, mas recusar a bandeira do cartão, pode haver uma falha de integração entre as operadoras, um problema técnico ou descumprimento das novas regras .

Segundo Elber, o trabalhador deve registrar a data e o local da tentativa de pagamento e, se possível, guardar a mensagem de erro exibida na maquininha.

Essas informações podem ajudar o trabalhador a registrar uma reclamação na operadora do cartão, no setor de recursos humanos da empresa ou em órgãos de defesa do consumidor.

A expectativa é que as recusas diminuam com a implementação completa da interoperabilidade, embora falhas pontuais ainda possam ocorrer durante a adaptação ao novo sistema.

O estabelecimento pode cobrar taxa extra ou exigir valor mínimo?

Não. Cobrar uma taxa extra pelo uso do vale-refeição ou do vale-alimentação, ou exigir um valor mínimo para aceitar o pagamento, é considerado prática abusiva.

A regra vale para cartões de todas as operadoras. O consumidor não pode ser prejudicado por escolher pagar uma compra com vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação.

Se isso acontecer, a orientação é guardar provas da cobrança ou da exigência e procurar os órgãos de defesa do consumidor.

Não. As mudanças não alteram os valores que as empresas depositam nos cartões de vale-refeição e vale-alimentação.

O valor dos benefícios continuará sendo definido pelas empresas ou pelas convenções e acordos coletivos de cada categoria profissional.

Representantes de restaurantes, supermercados e outros estabelecimentos reclamam há anos das taxas cobradas pelas operadoras e da demora para receber os valores pagos com vale-refeição e vale-alimentação.

Esses custos faziam com que muitos pequenos estabelecimentos considerassem pouco vantajoso aceitar cartões de determinadas operadoras.

As novas regras limitaram a 3,6% as taxas cobradas pelas operadoras dos estabelecimentos e determinaram que os valores das vendas sejam repassados em até 15 dias corridos.

Além disso, a interoperabilidade diminui a necessidade de contratar diferentes soluções de pagamento e permite que os estabelecimentos atendam trabalhadores que utilizam cartões de várias operadoras.

Segundo especialistas, as mudanças podem melhorar o fluxo de caixa dos estabelecimentos, facilitando o pagamento das despesas do dia a dia, e tornar a aceitação dos benefícios mais vantajosa para os comerciantes.

As empresas são obrigadas a fornecer vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação?

Não. Em geral, a obrigação de oferecer vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação depende de acordos ou convenções coletivas de trabalho, ou de regras internas adotadas pelas empresas.

Portanto, as mudanças no PAT alteram principalmente a forma como os benefícios são utilizados, mas não criam uma obrigação geral para que todas as empresas passem a oferecê-los.

Quem descumprir as regras pode ser multado?

Sim. Segundo a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, quem descumprir as regras previstas na legislação e na regulamentação do programa poderá sofrer penalidades administrativas.

As penalidades podem ser aplicadas a operadoras, estabelecimentos comerciais e outros participantes do sistema, conforme o tipo de irregularidade.

O objetivo é garantir que o dinheiro destinado à alimentação dos trabalhadores seja utilizado corretamente e que as demais regras do programa sejam respeitadas.

A Lei nº 6.321 prevê multas que variam de R$ 5 mil a R$ 50 mil. As multas podem ser dobradas em caso de reincidência ou quando houver tentativa de dificultar a fiscalização.

Além das multas, outras penalidades administrativas podem ser aplicadas, dependendo da gravidade da irregularidade.

Empresas cadastradas no PAT precisam fazer alguma atualização?

Sim. Além das novas regras para os cartões, empresas e profissionais inscritos no PAT também precisam ficar atentos a uma obrigação de atualização cadastral.

Segundo a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, nutricionistas, empresas beneficiárias, fornecedoras e facilitadoras cadastradas no PAT têm até 9 de novembro de 2026 para atualizar seus dados no novo sistema do programa.

O recadastramento é obrigatório independentemente das mudanças na aceitação dos cartões e deve ser realizado na plataforma disponibilizada pelo governo.

Quem não fizer o recadastramento dentro do prazo será excluído automaticamente do PAT e precisará solicitar uma nova inscrição para voltar ao programa.

articles.title: Quinto dia útil de novembro de 2026: veja a data do pagamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de novembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.summary: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de novembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.body:
Carteira de trabalho — Foto: Geraldo Bubniak/AEN

Para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de novembro de 2026 cai na sexta-feira, dia 6 . A data é o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário referente ao mês anterior, setembro, conforme as regras da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) .

Na contagem do prazo para o pagamento dos salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil. Já domingos e feriados não entram na contagem.

A regra está prevista no artigo 459 da CLT, que determina que o salário mensal deve ser pago, no máximo, até o quinto dia útil do mês seguinte ao trabalhado.

Quando é o quinto dia útil de outubro de 2026?

No cálculo do prazo para pagamento do salário, são considerados os dias de segunda-feira a sábado. Domingos e feriados ficam fora da contagem. Em novembro de 2026, a sequência será:

Primeiro dia útil: 2 de outubro (quinta-feira);

Segundo dia útil: 3 de outubro (sexta-feira);

Terceiro dia útil: 4 de outubro (sábado);

Quarto dia útil: 5 de outubro (segunda-feira);

Quinto dia útil: 6 de outubro (terça-feira).

Portanto, para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de novembro de 2026 é 6 de novembro.

Sábado conta como dia útil para o pagamento do salário?

Sim. Para a contagem do prazo previsto na CLT para o pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil.

A contagem é interrompida aos domingos e feriados. Por isso, mesmo que o trabalhador não tenha expediente aos sábados, o dia entra no cálculo do quinto dia útil.

Essa regra é específica para o prazo de pagamento do salário e não significa que o sábado seja necessariamente um dia normal de trabalho para todos os empregados.

Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de novembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário. — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

O que acontece se o salário não for pago até o quinto dia útil?

O artigo 459 da CLT estabelece o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário. Se o empregador não cumprir a data-limite, o trabalhador pode buscar orientação para cobrar os valores atrasados.

Em caso de atraso, o empregado pode recorrer à Justiça do Trabalho para cobrar o pagamento devido, com os acréscimos que forem aplicáveis. O sindicato da categoria também pode auxiliar na defesa dos direitos dos trabalhadores e na adoção das medidas cabíveis.

Atrasos frequentes ou prolongados no pagamento podem caracterizar descumprimento das obrigações do empregador.

Dependendo das circunstâncias e da gravidade da situação, isso pode levar ao reconhecimento da rescisão indireta, quando o trabalhador encerra o contrato por falta grave do empregador e pode ter direito às verbas de uma demissão sem justa causa.

O empregador também pode estar sujeito à fiscalização e às penalidades previstas na legislação trabalhista.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi: India's opposition rallies against voter roll revision exercise
articles.summary: It comes amid growing protests over a voter roll revision exercise feared to leave 130 million voters off rolls.
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of people are expected to gather in the Indian capital, Delhi, for a mega opposition rally, seeking the resignation of chief election commissioner and electoral reforms.

The rally, called by the main opposition Congress party, will begin around noon at the famous Ramlila Maidan grounds, with leaders claiming a million people could attend.

Several top leaders of the Congress-led INDIA alliance have said they would attend and the influential Gen Z-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has also pledged support.

The rally comes amid growing criticism of a voter-list revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from the draft rolls across India.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) says the exercise is aimed at updating the voters' list by purging names of people who have died or moved away from their registered addresses.

But opposition parties allege that the exercise - known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) - could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing eligible voters from the rolls. They accuse the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the BJP of "vote chori (theft)". Both the BJP and the ECI have denied the allegations.

The controversy intensified in September when The Indian Express newspaper in its investigation reported that the CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, made key decisions related to the exercise without the agreement of the two other election commissioners, who had raised objections on more than a dozen occasions.

The Election Commission said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.

But concerns over the revision process have continued, with the opposition parties, the CJP and student groups organising a number of protests in Delhi and other Indian cities.

On Saturday, opposition leaders staged a symbolic impeachment of Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in Delhi.

The mock parliamentary session, presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, saw leaders accuse the election chief of "conspiring to steal elections" and deliberately removing 130 million voters from electoral rolls.

Kharge, who is also the leader of the opposition in parliament's upper house, moved a symbolic motion seeking Kumar's removal, accusing him of undermining the electoral process and committing an act of "treason against the nation and the Constitution of India".

Several people whose names had been removed from electoral rolls during the revision exercise also attended the event.

The proceedings were purely symbolic and had no legal standing. Under Indian law, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a formal parliamentary process.

Prime Minister Modi has not directly commented on the mock impeachment proceedings. However, speaking at a public rally on Friday, he said that "some people" wanted to create chaos across the country so that he could be defamed.

Later on Saturday, while addressing a separate rally, he also accused opposition parties of "abandoning their duty" and "tearing apart the dignity and boundaries of the constitution".

Last month, Congress MP and leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi led tens of thousands of protesters in a march from Connaught Place in central Delhi to the Supreme Court, seeking the CEC's resignation.

"The march was just the trailer," a party leader told the BBC, adding that "Sunday's rally will be several times bigger than that".

Ahead of the rally, Gandhi said their protest was against "the demolition of Indian democracy", adding that "all the opposition parties and everybody who wants to come, political or non-political, is welcome".

"There is huge anger, huge emotional pain because millions are being disenfranchised," he said.

"We are all standing together because we are defending the Constitution. We are defending the idea of India. We are defending the vote, which is the expression of all Indians."

Delhi police have given permission to hold Sunday's rally, but it comes with several conditions. Media reports say the rally must end by 5pm, CCTV cameras must be installed at the venue and no marches will be allowed outside the designated protest site.

The planned mega rally has also divided opinion among traders in Chandni Chowk, one of Delhi's oldest and busiest markets, located less than a kilometre from Ramlila Maidan.

Earlier this week, a group of traders said the protest could hurt business during the festive season, coming just a week before Diwali.

But a rival group of traders said they supported Gandhi's rally and criticised the BJP for taking out a march through the market on Thursday, saying that disrupted the festive season more.

Authorities have deployed thousands of police and paramilitary personnel across the city, including the roads leading up to Ramlila Grounds, Sunday's protest venue.

The opposition, which has been preparing for the rally for days now, has accused the government of trying to stop people from travelling to Delhi to take part in the protest.

Rahul Gandhi has appealed to people to turn up in large numbers. "Don't worry about the police, don't worry about lathis [batons] - the BJP will not have the guts to try any of their antics," he wrote on X.

His comments come amid growing concerns about the policing of recent protests in the capital.

On 10 October, thousands of security personnel were deployed and large parts of the city were shut down to thwart protests called by the CJP against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

All of the top CJP leaders were detained and many demonstrators were beaten and dragged through the streets to break up their protests. BBC reporters covering demonstrations saw police dragging away protesters and using batons on some of them.

The CJP has publicly backed the INDIA bloc rally, but it is unclear whether its senior leaders will attend.

articles.title: UK weather: Fog to create hazardous driving conditions into next week
articles.summary: England and Wales are most likely to experience the foggy conditions on Sunday, before the threat shifts northwards into next week.
articles.body:
Dense fog will blanket parts of the UK on Sunday and into next week, causing dangerous driving conditions.

England and Wales are most likely to experience the foggy conditions on Sunday, before the threat shifts northwards into next week.

It comes after the Met Office issued a yellow weather warning for parts of England and Wales early on Saturday morning with visibility on roads predicted to drop to less than 100m in places.

Further warnings could be issued in the coming days as the waning strength of the late autumn sun means mist, fog and patches of low cloud are slow to clear.

Fog risk to shift northwards into next week

On Sunday morning the areas most at risk of seeing dense fog patches are parts of the Midlands, east Wales and eastern England. Some patchy mist and fog could form elsewhere too.

A weak weather front will bring a band of cloud and light drizzle over southern Scotland, northern England and the far north of Wales meaning these areas should have less chance of fog first thing on Sunday.

Brighter weather will develop more widely across Scotland and Northern Ireland and apart from the odd shower, many places here will enjoy spells of autumn sunshine.

From Monday onward, high pressure will remain the dominant weather system with the threat of fog shifting northwards.

As skies clear overnight and winds remain light, mist and fog patches will readily form, and combine with some slightly cooler nights and following days.

However as the high pressure drifts out into the North Sea, the wind across the south of the UK will change direction and strengthen.

Between Monday and Friday, the weather will not change very much at all.

The areas most prone to dense fog during the morning commutes this week are the Scottish glens, the Central Belt, the Cheshire Plains, the Vale of York and parts of Northern Ireland. However, some patches of mist and fog cannot be ruled out elsewhere too.

Disruption to travel is possible as the fog patches may be slow to clear from some places.

Though the UK will remain largely dry under high pressure, the east or northeast wind could introduce a few showers to eastern and southern coastal counties.

While daytime temperatures will remain close to average for early November, prolonged areas of fog and low cloud may keep some locations feeling noticeably cooler during the day.

Maximum temperatures during the afternoons will range from 11 to 14C north to south.

Meanwhile overnight lows will fall to 2 or 3C in the north, and around 5 to 8C further south.

With high pressure showing little sign of moving away, this largely settled and dry weather pattern looks set to continue through early November, with little prospect of any significant rainfall.

articles.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against WSJ over Epstein birthday book
articles.summary: Trump had sued the media outlet after it published a letter to Epstein purportedly written and signed by the president as part of a birthday book.
articles.body:
A US judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's $10bn dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal, ruling the suit was "grasping at straws".

Trump had sued the media outlet's parent company Dow Jones and its leader Rupert Murdoch last year after it reported on a letter allegedly written by Trump to disgraced financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein as part of a birthday book in 2003, before Epstein was charged with sex crimes.

Trump has denied writing or signing the letter, which included suggestive language and a drawing of the outline of a woman's body.

Judge Darrin Gayles threw out the case, finding the suit runs counter to the First Amendment, which protects freedom of the press.

Gayles had already once dismissed the defamation lawsuit, which sought $20 billion in damages. Trump's team refiled the suit seeking $10 billion, and this time, the judge threw out the case "with prejudice," meaning the suit cannot be filed again.

The news outlet's story about Epstein's 50th birthday book - and the letter with Trump's name - came as the Trump administration battled intense bipartisan criticism over the summer for its handling of Epstein documents.

Trump had said the newspaper had slandered him and violated libel laws in publishing the article.

In his 20-page ruling, Gayles noted the paper's "thoughtful and detailed ​investigation" that led to the story and said the lawsuit was "grasping at ‌straws" to "to manufacture flaws" their work.

The judge wrote that Trump's legal team did not prove that the defendants made defamatory statements with "actual malice", which the law requires be proven.

Actual malice is high bar to meet, as it requires proof that the defendant knew the defamatory statement was false or acted with reckless disregard for whether it was true or not.

Trump alleged that the letter obtained and released by the Journal, which features his signature at the bottom, was "fake" and that the defendants devised the story in order to defame him.

Trump's legal team had argued that because Trump denied writing the letter when contacted by the Journal, the paper should have "disregarded everything else they learned in their investigation and not published the story", Gayles wrote.

"But that is not what the actual malice standard requires and runs afoul of the First Amendment," Gayles wrote.

If that were the law, he wrote, then "any time a public figure or his team denies an accusation, journalists would be immediately blocked from publishing negative or contradictory press—a result that flies in the face of the 'American privilege to speak one's mind'".

According to the Wall Street Journal story, a letter bearing Trump's name "contained several lines of typewritten text framed by the outline of a naked woman, which appears to be hand-drawn with a heavy marker".

It reportedly contained a joking reference that "enigmas never age" and allegedly ended with the words: "A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday - and may every day be another wonderful secret".

articles.title: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent
articles.summary: Police in Frankfurt say "violent riots" took place in the city centre, with unrest also reported in Berlin, Hamburg and Cologne.
articles.body:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday and clashes erupted with police there and in other German cities after largely peaceful mass protests over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who targeted emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands earlier joined the demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.

The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police, AFP news agency reported. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".

She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."

Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?

While protests during the day were largely peaceful, the demonstrations turned violent as night fell.

In a post on X, Frankfurt police said that "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.

In later updates, officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect.

Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.

Poseck said: "We all have those images from France in our minds – looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."

articles.title: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: In a counterprotest, Netanyahu supporters demand that Israel should not have a government with ‘terrorists’.
articles.body:
Thousands of people have rallied in Tel Aviv to urge the Israeli opposition to make a deal with Arab parties to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Protesters at Saturday’s rally told the AFP news agency this may be the “last chance for real change” and that Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, is a “great manipulator”.

Main opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has previously ruled out forming a coalition with Israel’s Arab parties, but a deadlock in Tuesday’s elections means siding with the parties could help him form a government.

“People really want this vote for change to work out, and they believe that… Gadi Eisenkot and other leaders of the Jewish-Israeli parties need to listen to their voice,” Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh said from Ramallah on Saturday.

Counter-protesters also showed up to Saturday’s demonstrations, with Netanyahu supporters seen shouting their own demands that “Israel should not have a government with so-called terrorists”, Odeh said.

Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday’s elections, while Eisenkot’s won 48, meaning neither side can form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament alone.

Israel’s three Arab-led parties won 19 seats, having made significant gains in Tuesday’s election.

Nearly 840,000 people voted for Ra’am and the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab-led parties, a 64 percent increase from the last elections in 2022, according to the Central Election Committee.

The Arab electoral success means a coalition with Eisenkot would provide a comfortable majority of 67. However, for many in Israel, the idea of siding with Arabs is politically unpalatable.

Netanyahu has accused Palestinian-Israeli parties of “stealing” the polls and accepting funding from Qatar to do it. Qatar has rejected the allegations , calling it a disinformation campaign.

Odeh said that Israeli right-wing circles have described “the historic turnout of Palestinian Israelis as electoral terrorism, equating it to the October 7th attack”, when Hamas-led fighters stormed southern Israel, killing more than 1,200 people and taking hundreds captive.

“Palestinian-Israeli votes and voices” are under attack because they have a “prominent position” in deciding whether Eisenkot can form a government, she added.

articles.title: FBI links North Korean hackers to biggest crypto heist in history; Trump questions claim
articles.summary: The FBI has blamed North Korean hackers for the theft of $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, in what is
articles.body: The FBI has blamed North Korean hackers for the theft of $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, in what is being described as the biggest crypto heist in history. However, US President Donald Trump has said investigators are yet to establish whether Pyongyang was behind the attack.In a statement on Saturday, the FBI linked the attack to “malicious cyber activity” by a group identified as TraderTraitor. The same group was also held responsible for a $1.5 billion hack targeting crypto exchange Bybit last year.According to the FBI, TraderTraitor has been converting the stolen assets primarily into Ethereum. Investigators expect the hackers to use decentralised finance (DeFi) platforms and instant cryptocurrency swap services to move the funds and conceal their origins, AP reported.However, Trump appeared to cast doubt on the attribution when questioned by reporters during a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday night.“I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it,” Trump said, adding that investigators did not yet know whether North Korea was involved. He did not rule out the possibility that the country could eventually be identified as responsible.Ari Redbord, chief policy officer at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, said the hackers could split the stolen cryptocurrency into smaller amounts and route it through multiple exchanges to avoid detection. The laundering process could continue for months, he said.“It’s bank robbery, in this case, at the speed of the Internet,” Redbord said, adding that blockchain technology also allows investigators to track the movement of stolen funds in real time, potentially helping them disrupt transactions and recover the money.The $6.3 billion theft, involving Bitcoin and other digital currencies, came to light on Thursday. Several cryptocurrency experts had earlier pointed to indicators suggesting North Korean involvement.Binance said on Saturday that it had sufficient reserves in the same digital currencies that were stolen to cover 90% of the missing assets. articles.title: Meet William Alexander Charouhis, Florida student whose initiative led to the planting of more than 2,289 mangroves after Hurricane Irma flooded his hometown
articles.summary: When Hurricane Irma flooded Miami, Florida, William Alexander Charouhis experienced firsthand how extreme weather can affect coastal communities.
articles.body: When Hurricane Irma flooded Miami, Florida, William Alexander Charouhis experienced firsthand how extreme weather can affect coastal communities. The flooding inspired him to take action by protecting mangrove trees, which play an important role in coastal defence and carbon sequestration. He started an initiative called One Million Mangroves to conserve and restore these trees. According to the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), his project has resulted in the planting of more than 2,289 mangroves across six miles of Florida coastline. The initiative has also organised community clean-ups involving more than 120 volunteers. Through these efforts, William has worked to protect mangrove habitats and raise awareness about their importance in coastal areas.Hurricane Irma inspired William to launch One Million MangrovesHurricane Irma flooded William's hometown of Miami, Florida, giving him firsthand experience of the effects of extreme weather on a community. Coastal areas are particularly exposed to such events, which can damage property, displace millions of people, and threaten natural ecosystems.The experience led William to develop One Million Mangroves, an initiative focused on conserving and restoring mangrove trees. These trees play an important role in protecting coastal areas and storing carbon. His project focuses on using mangrove conservation as a nature-based approach to address climate change. Through the initiative, William set out to support coastal communities by restoring trees that provide important environmental benefits.More than 2,289 mangroves planted across six miles of Florida coastlineOne Million Mangroves has resulted in the planting of more than 2,289 mangroves across six miles of Florida coastline. The project focuses on conserving and restoring mangrove trees, which provide coastal protection and help with carbon sequestration.Alongside planting activities, the initiative has organised community clean-ups to remove litter from mangrove root systems. More than 120 volunteers have taken part in these activities. Removing litter from the root systems gives the plants a better chance to thrive. The clean-ups form another part of the project's efforts to support mangrove conservation. Together, the planting work and volunteer activities focus on restoring mangroves and protecting the coastal environments.How did William raise awareness about mangrove protectionWilliam also took his conservation work beyond mangrove planting by speaking about the initiative and the importance of mangrove protection. He shared his efforts at the 2023 Miami Youth Climate Summit, where he spoke to hundreds of students, business leaders, and government leaders.The event gave him an opportunity to explain the importance of protecting mangroves and discuss the work carried out through One Million Mangroves. articles.title: Quad must safeguard freedom of choice and secure supply chains, says Jaishankar
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday highlighted freedom of choice, secure supply chains and tackling non-market practices as key areas of
articles.body: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday highlighted freedom of choice, secure supply chains and tackling non-market practices as key areas of focus for the Quad, while calling for a modern and action-oriented approach to the grouping's priorities.In a post on X after the Quad foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar outlined the major issues discussed with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian foreign minister Penny Wong."Maintaining stability, driving prosperity and ensuring freedom of choice as our continuing commitments in the Indo-Pacific," Jaishankar said, describing these as the grouping's ongoing objectives.He stressed the importance of deeper cooperation to develop resilient supply chains and strengthen security in the technology, critical minerals and energy sectors.The external affairs minister also highlighted the need to address "non-market practices and increased economic stresses in the Indo-Pacific" as part of the discussions. However, he did not name any country or elaborate on the specific practices being referenced.On regional security, Jaishankar called for greater progress on existing cooperation agreements covering counter-terrorism, maritime security and capacity building, with the aim of strengthening regional resilience and promoting peace and stability.He also emphasised the importance of "developing a more contemporary QUAD agenda with a practical approach".Quad announces initiatives on AI, critical mineralsThe joint statement issued after the meeting outlined several measures to expand economic and security cooperation among the four countries.The ministers expressed their intention to provide more than $85 million in technical and financial support to improve access to trusted artificial intelligence across the Indo-Pacific region. The initiative will also be supported through the Quad AI Accelerator.The statement also mentioned "Super Intelligence", with a footnote explaining that the term refers to artificial intelligence in India, Australia and Japan.The ministers welcomed the US commitment of $10 million towards developing facilities in India and ASEAN countries to recover critical minerals from waste. The funding is intended to support facilities across the region and is not exclusively earmarked for India.The four countries are looking to recover valuable minerals from discarded electronic equipment and scrap materials to reduce reliance on individual suppliers. They will also examine ways to simplify cross-border transportation of recyclable materials.Maritime security and regional cooperationAs part of their maritime collaboration, officials from all four Quad countries undertook a voyage aboard an Indian Coast Guard offshore patrol vessel from Chennai to Perth between September 25 and October 7.The partners are also working towards their first exercise under the Indo-Pacific maritime surveillance collaboration initiative, scheduled to take place during Sea Dragon 2027. A maritime domain awareness symposium is additionally planned for early next year.The ministers also committed to tackling online scam networks and ensuring accountability for transnational criminal organisations. They condemned groups involved in human trafficking and forcing victims to participate in fraudulent activities.Another major announcement was the launch of the first Quad Business Leaders' Forum, which aims to deepen commercial engagement and create fresh business opportunities across strategic sectors.The meeting in Atlanta took place on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting and marked the third Quad ministerial engagement this year, following earlier gatherings in New Delhi and Manila.The Quad comprises India, the United States, Japan and Australia. articles.title: Chandigarh couple pays Rs 62.7 lakh, nearly 95% of flat cost, but builder repeatedly delays possession for 2 years, he then stops monthly compensation and issues possession letter despite apartment lacking fire safety certificate. Now, consumer commission orders refund with 12% interest and Rs 1.1 lakh compensation and costs
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: A real estate firm and its two directors have been directed to refund Rs 62.7 lakh with 12% annual interest to a Zirakpur homebuyer couple
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: A real estate firm and its two directors have been directed to refund Rs 62.7 lakh with 12% annual interest to a Zirakpur homebuyer couple after repeatedly delaying possession of their flat, stopping monthly compensation and issuing a possession letter despite the apartment lacking a fire safety certificate.The State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, UT Chandigarh, also ordered the builder to pay Rs 75,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 35,000 towards litigation costs within 30 days, holding the firm guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices.Saurabh Verma and his wife, Puja Rani, booked a 1,590-square-foot apartment for Rs 66.5 lakh in October 2022, with possession originally scheduled for October 31, 2023. They paid Rs 62.7 lakh, including Rs 40.1 lakh through a home loan, but the developer failed to deliver the flat within the agreed period.The builder subsequently extended the possession deadline three times, in September 2023, August 2024 and August 2025. The revised deadlines were November 2024, July 2025 and December 31, 2025.The firm initially paid the couple Rs 30,000 per month as compensation for the delay, but stopped making the payments after a year. The commission directed that the compensation paid between November 2023 and November 2024 be adjusted against the final refund.Possession letter issued despite missing fire safety certificateThe couple alleged that the builder demanded additional money for finishing work despite the slow pace of construction. They claimed the firm threatened to cancel the contract and charge 24% interest if they failed to make the payments.On September 27, 2025, the developer issued a possession letter, which the buyers refused to accept, citing incomplete construction and the absence of mandatory statutory approvals.An RTI response dated January 2, 2026, confirmed that the apartment lacked a fire safety certificate, according to the complaint.The commission observed that issuing a possession letter without the required statutory clearances did not establish that a residential unit was fit for occupation. It also noted that the builder's defence was struck off on April 16, 2026, after the firm failed to file its written reply within the prescribed 45-day period.Buyers cannot be made to wait indefinitelyRelying on Supreme Court precedents, the commission held that homebuyers could not be compelled to wait indefinitely for possession or accept an incomplete apartment."The obligation of a builder is not merely to construct a structure or issue a letter describing possession as offered; it is to deliver the contracted residential unit within the stipulated period, in a habitable condition and in conformity with the applicable statutory requirements," the commission observed.It held that repeated delays, discontinuation of compensation and demands for additional funds amounted to material deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.The commission also highlighted that the couple had paid nearly 95% of the flat's total cost, leaving a substantial portion of their financial resources tied up in a property whose lawful and habitable possession had not been established.The builder and its two directors have been directed to refund Rs 62.7 lakh with 12% annual interest calculated from the respective dates of deposit. articles.title: Ohio State's national title hopes are rightfully fading after USC delivers reality check in shocking upset
articles.summary: Lincoln Riley's USC upset over No. 2 Ohio State exposes the Buckeyes' offensive collapse, with Oregon, Nebraska and Michigan still on the schedule.
articles.body: If the Big Ten was resting their hopes on Ohio State being able to put together an offense capable of contending for a national championship, then Saturday night's 30-18 loss to USC was a reality check on the current situation. Following the unfortunate loss of starting quarterback Julian Sayin to an elbow injury during the Indiana game two weeks ago, the fate of the Buckeyes season rested on the arms of Luke Fahey and freshman Taven St. Clair. The nervousness around Columbus has been rampant since that day in Bloomington, and rightfully so given that Ryan Day had pinned his offensive hopes around the quarterback being able to disrupt opposing defenses with the Julian Sayin to Jeremiah Smith connection. GOOD LUCK, SEC: AUBURN AWOKE A MONSTER IN ATHENS, AND FLORIDA PAYS THE PRICE IN GEORGIA’S COCKTAIL BEATDOWN This pair opened up so many options for an offense that essentially forced opposing teams to decide on whether double-teaming the star wide receiver was worth the risk in losing a defender in the secondary. Even with 484 yards of total offense against USC on Saturday night, it was the offensive line that struggled to protect quarterback Luke Fahey, while also not capitalizing inside the red zone. You might ask whether one player is worth that much attention. To that, most college football fans would just implore you to "watch the tape" on the former Heisman Trophy leader coming out of the Indiana showdown that saw the Buckeyes leave Bloomington with a very important win. Now, a few weeks later, there are rightful questions about this Ohio State team moving forward over the next month, along with where the Big Ten stands as we await the first CFP rankings of the 2026 season. The answer to that question centered around the fact Ohio State had not scored a touchdown against USC through three quarters, and they looked like a squad who was lost on offense for a majority of this upset loss. OHIO STATE QB JULIAN SAYIN'S INJURY MAY COMPLETELY RESHAPE THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RACE Does Ohio State look like a national title contender without Julian Sayin? No, not right now after two weeks of preparation for the trip to Los Angeles. If anything, the Buckeyes look like a team that would be on the brink of missing the playoff tonight if Indiana were to have somehow won that intense showdown. So yes, Ohio State fans are clearly entering the panic mode of what could have been if Julian Sayin were to not have been injured. Also, let's not forget the other unfortunate part of this problem for the Buckeyes. Entering the matchup with Indiana, Jeremiah Smith was the proverbial leader in the clubhouse for the Heisman Trophy. Now, he's going to need plenty of superman-like efforts to have his name called in New York City next month, without a quarterback capable enough to get him the ball downfield. COLLEGE FOOTBALL CHAOS: HISTORIC UPSETS, ARCH MANNING'S FIASCO, CLOCK CONTROVERSY AND CFP RAMIFICATIONS ARISE Sure, we know Smith is a man of high character and is more worried about the wins and losses. But, let's not act as though the situation isn’t a brutal dose of reality that his campaign might have ended in Bloomington. Fittingly, it was Jeremiah Smith who scored Ohio State's first touchdown of the night with 2:12 remaining in the game on a five-yard out in the end zone. As for Ohio State moving forward, there is nothing about their performance against USC that should give the CFP committee enough evidence to put them in the top-12 on Tuesday night. We all remember when Florida State was left out of the national championship game after Jordan Travis went down with a knee injury, right? No, we aren’t at that point just yet, but we're getting there. Over the next five weeks, Ohio State will face Northwestern, Oregon, Nebraska and Michigan. INDIANA SURVIVES MINNESOTA SCARE WITH SECOND STRAIGHT OVERTIME WIN TO KEEP NATIONAL TITLE DEFENSE ALIVE Are we going to act as though this Buckeyes offense is good enough to avoid another loss? Sure, you can make that argument, but Oregon and Northwestern are talented enough to beat them in Columbus, and Nebraska is so awkward that it could have a lead heading into the fourth quarter. The Buckeyes defense isn’t strong enough to carry them through the month of November, especially if this is what they are going to get from the offensive side of the ball. And unfortunately, Jeremiah Smith and running back Bo Jackson can't do it all without a viable quarterback that oozes confidence. Lincoln Riley finds himself on the winning side, with a tough stretch ahead Give credit where it's due with this USC football team. Coming off a loss to Wisconsin this week, with reasonable conversations surrounding his job status with the Trojans, the talk of Riley coaching somewhere else next season started picking up enough that he could not avoid the questions over the past five days. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Now, there is at least a path to the postseason, though it won't be an easy one. After a week off, USC will play Indiana on the road, followed by a game against Maryland, before ending the season with a crosstown showdown with UCLA. Can they run the table? Sure, if this is the type of performance we get over the next month. But, even with the win over Ohio State, it's still hard to trust the Trojans. They’re going to have to prove it.

articles.title: UN demands investigation after staffer’s death in Houthi custody in Yemen
articles.summary: Mohammad el-Shami had been held since June 2024, when he and many other UN and NGO workers were accused of being spies.
articles.body:
The United Nations has demanded an investigation into the death of an employee in Houthi detention in Yemen.

Mohammad el-Shami, a staff member of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in Yemen, died more than a month ago, but his family was only recently informed, the UN said in a statement on Saturday.

The Houthis did not say how he died, but his family “deserve to know the truth”, said UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk.

The human rights chief also demanded “full transparency” from the Houthi authorities and an “urgent, independent and thorough investigation” into el-Shami’s death.

El-Shami had been arbitrarily held in Houthi custody since June 2024, when he and more than 60 people working with the UN and other NGOs were detained and accused of being part of an “American-Israeli spy network”.

“I am also gravely concerned” for the seven other OHCHR personnel who were detained alongside el-Shami and are still being held, Turk said. “I appeal again for their immediate and unconditional release.”

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said in a separate statement on Saturday that he was “appalled” by el-Shami’s death and echoed Turk’s calls for an investigation.

The UN is “urgently seeking answers” from the group about the circumstances of his death, Guterres added.

El-Shami is the second UN staff member to die in Houthi detention, following the death of a World Food Programme staffer in February 2025.

A total of 72 UN staffers and NGO workers, including el-Shami, have been detained by the Houthis.

The UN paused operations in parts of Houthi-held Yemen in February 2025 over concerns for the safety of its employees.

The rebel group has previously paraded some detainees on television channels, presenting them as collaborators with Western intelligence agencies and Israel.

On October 6, the UN announced that a World Food Programme employee had been released after being “arbitrarily detained” by the Iran-backed group.

articles.title: Italian taxpayers are paying millions to keep Russian yachts afloat
articles.summary: An expensive floating eyesore has marred views in the port of Trieste, northern Italy, for more than four years, and it is costing Italian taxpayers millions to maintain, the city’s mayor says.
articles.body: An expensive floating eyesore has marred views in the port of Trieste, northern Italy, for more than four years, and it is costing Italian taxpayers millions to maintain, the city’s mayor says. Russian oligarch Andrey Igorevich Melnichenko’s “Sailing Yacht A,” one of the world’s largest sailing vessels and worth around $600 million, was in Trieste for maintenance in March 2022 when Russia’s invasion of Ukraine led to widespread sanctions and seizures of Russian assets. Among them was Melnichenko’s 468-foot craft, once dubbed the “world’s ugliest yacht” and known simply as “A” by locals who have grown to hate it. Designed by Philippe Starck, the superyacht features an outer surface that is ghostlike, its barely visible windows embedded in a shimmering armored steel frame. Its three rotating carbon masts are as tall as an eight-story palazzo, casting a silhouette that has by now become a fixture in the busy port where dozens of cruise ships dock each week. In September 2025, Mayor Roberto Dipiazza raised the issue of who is paying for the yacht’s mooring fees and maintenance in a public campaign, calling it a “disgrace,” and threatening to sell it or sail it away. Dipiazza told CNN that the cost to keep the ship afloat, including paying for a 20-person crew, fuel to run the generators, specialized cleaning, security and insurance, amounts to around $30,000 a day – or nearly $11 million a year. According to Italian law, a sequestered ship must be maintained and cannot be left to rust or sink. If and when sanctions against Melnichenko are lifted, he will have to pay back those costs to retrieve his vessel. “It will eventually cost him less to buy a new yacht than to pay back all we have spent,” Dipazza said. “And where does that leave us? We could be paying for this monstrosity for years.” Melnichenko, a banker and industrialist whose fortune is estimated at around $20 billion, challenged the seizure of the yacht in the summer of 2022, arguing that the vessel was not directly owned by him, but instead a company called Valla Sails through a trust set up by his wife. The case was heard by a court in Rome in 2022 and eventually reached the Court of Justice of the European Union, which ruled in 2025 that Italy has the right to keep it sequestered – and with it, the obligation to maintain it. Sailing Yacht A is not the only Russian yacht costing Italians money. In the Tuscan port of Marina di Carrara, the six-deck, 465-foot superyacht Scheherazade is docked behind high walls to keep it both safe and hidden from curious onlookers. While it is reportedly licensed to Rosneft executive Eduard Khudainatov, Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny credibly claimed it actually belongs to Russian President Vladimir Putin. On August 28 of this year, it left the port heading north towards the Italian Rivieria, according to transponder signals recorded by Vessel Finder, heavily flanked by Italian security forces. It returned after ten hours of what a spokesperson for the Italian Sea Group, whose dock it is moored at, said were technical tests as part of its maintenance. The superyacht, worth $700 million, has twin helipads among its many amenities and a swimming pool that converts to a dance floor, according to Superyacht Times. The Scheherazade’s mooring contract had been paid through September, according to tax records seen by CNN. Italian Sea Group will not say who paid for, or who is now paying for, those mooring costs. Since it was sequestered, Tuscan taxpayers have paid more than $15 million for the skeleton crew, some of whom are British and others Russian, which switches out several times a year, according to local press reports. A film crew that tried to approach the vessel last year was chased away by drones and water canon. Additional costs include the security to make sure no one gets close – and that it doesn’t set sail while sequestered. Among the other vessels that Italy is paying to keep is the Lady M, a sleek 210-foot superyacht owned by Alexei Mordashov, a Putin associate and majority shareholder in Severstal, Russia’s largest steel and mining company. Forbes puts Mordashov’s net worth at nearly $37 billion. Lady M is sequestered in Imperia, and has cost Italian taxpayers around $2 million so far, Matteo Bonjean, vice director of the port of Marina di Imperia, told Forbes. The 126-foot superyacht Lena, owned by Gennady Timchenko, another Putin ally, is being maintained nearby. All of the sequestered vessels have crews that maintain the yachts, paid for by the Italian government. Other costs include the use of air conditioning to prevent mold from growing inside. Italy is by no means the only country stuck with costs for sequestered yachts in Europe. Germany has the $800 million Dilbar, owned at one time by the sister of sanctioned Russian magnate Alisher Usmanov. France is paying to keep the sanctioned oligarch Igor Sechin’s Amore Vera, and Spain maintains the Tango, owned by sanctioned Russian oligarch Viktor Vekselberg. Gibraltar was able to auction off Russian steel magnate Dmitry Pumpyansky’s 236-foot Axioma for some $37.5 million, according to Reuters. The United States has sold several vessels, including the Amadea, owned by twice-sanctioned Russian politician Suleiman Kerimov. Not all countries choose to pay upkeep if their national laws don’t require it. Sanctioned Russian Andrey Guryev’s massive 353-foot Luminosity, sequestered in Montenegro, has been left to rust and rot, according to images posted on social media by Benetti Yachts, which built the ship. Montenegro tried to sell the yacht in 2024 for €135 million, but the sale was ultimately blocked and the yacht continues to languish in the Porto Montenegro marina in Tivat. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has been a strong supporter of maintaining sanctions against Russian oligarchs tied to Putin, warning the Italian Senate last month that any softening or deal making with Moscow was “a very risky choice.” Many others, like Trieste mayor Dipiazza, feel that taxpayers should not have to pay for the upkeep of oligarchs’ toys.

articles.title: ‘Like Kashmir’: How a toxic marble dump yard became a tourist spot in India
articles.summary: Vast ‘snow yard’ in otherwise arid Rajasthan attracts hundreds of tourists daily, but residents face major health risks.
articles.body:
Kishangarh, India – As Bagharam Gurjar kneels to pull weeds from his maize field in western India’s Rajasthan state, the sound of his wife coughing nearby makes him restless.

“Everything gets ruined when dust settles on the soil,” says Gurjar, 53, barely looking up.

“May God make everything right,” replies his wife between bouts of chronic cough. “Otherwise, it becomes difficult to grow crops.”

The Gurjars are among nearly 5,000 people living in the vicinity of what has turned out to be one of the most unusual tourist destinations in India.

Their village, Bhogiyawas, is just 6km (4 miles) from Kishangarh, where a 300-acre (121-hectare) marble slurry dumping yard resembles a snow-clad landscape, attracting hundreds of tourists every day in an otherwise arid state.

Locally known as a “Snow Yard”, the landfill in Rajasthan’s Ajmer district is the largest of its kind in Asia. Its pristine white hills and slopes with water-filled pits provide a surreal backdrop for visitors, who get free entry to the site.

Newlyweds pose against the snowy backdrop or the blue artificial lake, while couples soon to get married organise pre-wedding photoshoots. Social media influencers throng the landfill to make reels. Music videos and movies are also frequently shot here.

“Everyone, right from my five-year-old niece to my mother, loves it very much. Their first impression was that this looks like Kashmir,” Salim Shahzada, a businessman from Uttar Pradesh state, told Al Jazeera, referring to Indian-administered Kashmir.

Shahzada said he had visited the place a couple of times and decided to bring his family along this time. But he had no idea about the health and environmental problems linked to the dumping yard.

“I do not have much knowledge about this place or its ill effects. I only know that this is where marble cutting waste is dumped and that the hill itself is made of this waste,” he said.

Kishangarh, a marble and granite hub, is home to nearly 1,200 processing units, with the total daily business estimated at more than 160 million rupees ($1.7m), providing jobs to about 25,000 people, according to the Federation of Indian Granite and Stone Industry.

Every day, nearly 1,000 tankers carry slurry from those units and empty roughly 5,500 tonnes of waste on the government-allotted dump site, which, for the people living nearby, has turned into a health hazard.

Gurjar said the yard has affected residents in at least six villages. “How many problems can I even tell you about? If there were just one or two, we could deal with them,” he said.

“But here, almost everything is going wrong because of the dumping yard. People like me are suffering from chest infections, dental problems and skin allergies. It does not matter whether they are children or elderly people; everyone is suffering.”

Gurjar said he and his wife are forced to take regular medicines for chest infections or skin problems.

Aditi Goyal, a general physician at Ajmer’s Ganga Narayan Hospital, said the residents of Kishangarh face several health risks, mainly respiratory and skin problems. She said the workers in the marble processing units are more vulnerable to chronic illnesses because of prolonged exposure to toxic dust.

“Over the last couple of years, cases of respiratory problems have increased significantly in this area because people are exposed to dust from the dumping yard,” Goyal told Al Jazeera.

“However, dust from industrial waste is not the only issue. People in Kishangarh, who are mostly farmers, also suffer from infections caused by dust coming from the soil,” she said, advising people to wear masks to protect themselves from dust.

The same dust settles on the fields, hardening the soil and making it difficult to grow crops.

A study led by Laxmi Kant Sharma, professor in the department of environmental science at the Central University of Rajasthan, found that the concentration of lead silicate in Kishangarh’s soil was several times higher than normal, indicating extreme contamination.

“Since the waste particles are smaller than 75 micrometres, they can spread far and wide, making the soil infertile,” the study said.

The study also found that the concentration of PM2.5 exceeds the limit of ambient air quality standards. “Several people may be suffering from silicosis. The government needs to take immediate action to prevent the situation from getting out of hand,” it said.

Ugam Singh, another resident of Bhogiyawas, remembers when things were different. The continuous dumping of slurry slowly changed the landscape and the lives of people in Kishangarh, says the 65-year-old.

“Nowadays, the situation has worsened to such an extent that even the groundwater is no longer fit for consumption,” Singh said.

“The fluoride levels in the water are so high that it tastes salty. My teeth have started decaying and my bones have become weak,” he added, pointing to his teeth, which appeared pale, pitted and worn.

Singh said the residents of villages surrounding the dump yard have complained to the authorities, including officials of the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board (RSPCB). But their requests fell on deaf ears.

“What I have come to understand is that it does not matter which government is in power. No one listens to the poor. To make the rich richer, the government sacrifices the interests of people like us. It feels as though our lives have no value,” Singh said.

“Even today all we want is for this marble slurry dumping to stop so that we can breathe freely again and our fields can become green and productive once again.”

Singh also claims that if residents of all the villages around the dumping yard were properly examined, almost every household would have someone suffering from respiratory problems such as asthma.

Last year, local environmentalist Drupad Malik filed a case before the National Green Tribunal over the harmful health and environmental effects of the Kishangarh dumping yard. The tribunal observed that unregulated dumping of marble slurry was contaminating groundwater and air. It directed the RSPCB to enforce monitoring, conduct sample inspections and penalise the marble processing units violating environmental norms.

Al Jazeera reached out to a senior official at the RSPCB’s regional office in Kishangarh, but she refused to speak on the matter.

Central University’s Sharma said the areas surrounding the Kishangarh dumping yard are unfit for human settlement. He said his research was shared with state authorities, but nothing was done to improve the environmental conditions in the area.

“There is a dire need to shift the dumping yard to another place where there is no human contact. This area has become extremely toxic and vulnerable to severe diseases. I am surprised that people are allowed to visit the site without masks and even have food there,” Sharma told Al Jazeera.

“I have forwarded several suggestions, including installing tile units, as [marble] slurry is used in tile manufacturing. This could, to some extent, help reduce pollution in Kishangarh,” he added.

Meanwhile, Ram Lal, a resident of Tokra village, about a 15-minute drive from Bhogiyawas, appealed to the government to find an alternative site for dumping the marble slurry.

“Kishangarh is full of slurry, and it is time to shift the dumping yard out of here to some other place where no one will suffer for at least two to three decades,” Lal told Al Jazeera.

“We also demand that free medical camps be set up to assess people whose health has declined because of the fine dust particles that have been flying in the air and settling here for years,” he said.

“No one from our village can afford it if someone develops a disease that costs thousands of rupees to treat.”

articles.title: The Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with gold; why the cracks are highlighted instead of hidden
articles.summary: The fast paced world that runs on short term trends, the Japanese people have been embracing the broken.
articles.body: The fast paced world that runs on short term trends, the Japanese people have been embracing the broken. As a reminder to embrace the imperfections, this Japanese traditional art brings together broken pieces of pottery to not just repair the damage but to highlight the defects. This art is called kintsugi, where lacquer and gold is used to restore broken pottery. Instead of disguising the cracks, the craft highlights them, turning the damage into something beautiful. What was once broken becomes a vessel with a new appearance, a richer story and, in many cases, an even more distinctive character.The idea presents a great contrast for the country where technology runs to achieve new feats everyday. While everyone is spending so much time trying to make everything look flawless, embracing the cracks is worth celebrating.What exactly is kintsugi?Kintsugi literally translates to “golden joinery” where kin means gold and tsugi means joining. It is also known as kintsukuroi which implies "golden repair". The tradition goes back to the 15th century and is closely associated with Japanese tea culture. The craft has endured for centuries where broken pottery is mended using a special lacquer called urushi, which is usually mixed with powdered gold.The process is more intricate than it seems while looking at the finished piece. It involves carefully collecting the ceramic fragments to combine them using the sap of the Japanese lacquer tree. The completed product seems almost intentional with unique gold designing over the cracks.It takes patience, precision and considerable skill. Traditional lacquer repairs can involve multiple stages, with time needed for each layer to cure. The result is a piece that retains its original form while wearing its repair openly, like a delicate golden map of everything it has been through.And gold is not the only possible finish. There are artisans that use silver, platinum and even mismatched ceramic fragments to create an entirely new appearance. This creates every piece with its own character, holding the artisan's vision at the forefront.Why highlight the cracks instead of hiding them?The idea behind embracing antiques like an old wooden table or a handwritten letter with faded ink is that they hold a story and human connection within their material existence. People often adore books that have turned yellow over the years, exchanging hands and locations because they have transformed minds over generations. These objects cannot be replaced by new collections as they lack history. Kintsugi applies that same sentiment to broken pottery.The golden seams do not attempt to conceal the cracks, rather they embrace the accident that happened. They become a beautiful part of the object’s identity even if the pottery may not return to its original shape and form. Kintsugi transforms the joints into an integral part of its appearance, giving it a new life while retaining the history behind it. And since no two broken objects fracture in exactly the same way, no two repairs can ever look alike.The philosophy behind the golden seamsKintsugi is often associated with wabi-sabi, a Japanese belief that finds beauty in imperfection and values simplicity. Instead of perfection, this philosophy allows us to embrace irregularities. This doctrine particularly holds importance in the traditional Japanese tea ceremonies where ceramic bowls have an important role to play. They have long been valued for their distinct character. A bowl's irregular glaze, handmade shape or visible signs of age can contribute to its appeal. Kintsugi extends that appreciation to breakage itself.There is an important distinction, though: kintsugi is a traditional craft with its own history and technical discipline, not simply a motivational metaphor. Its deeper meaning has been interpreted in different ways, and not every Japanese person or artisan necessarily understands it identically.A lesson in sustainability, tooIn an age when replacing a damaged object can seem easier than repairing it, kintsugi offers a quieter alternative: give something a second life.The technique comprises the spirit of reusing even when markets are flooded with new replacements. It encourages people to preserve objects rather than discarding them the moment they get a defect. With the world gaining a consciousness towards sustainability, the art has gained a renewed interest. Therefore, there are kintsugi workshops being held in recent times.The involvement of gold and intricate craftsmanship makes traditional kintsugi expensive and time-consuming. It is not necessarily the quickest or cheapest way to mend a broken cup.
